EXPERIENCE_LIST.EXPERIENCE_DESCRIPTION: I contribute to the development of digital solutions that optimize port logistics operations, building accessible, scalable, and user-centered interfaces with Angular and TypeScript, supported by technologies such as SCSS, RxJS, and custom component libraries. I integrate AI-assisted development tools into the workflow to accelerate development, refactoring, and code review tasks, maintaining high quality standards. I work in an agile environment, collaborating closely with analysts and backend developers to deliver robust, high-value solutions for the sector.

I build tools for AI agents and measure what they add, in my own projects and in open-source contributions. In rea I have 14 merged pull requests, which brought the real Ghidra verification on Windows back to green, moved the Claude Code and Gemini CLI checks and three MCP test suites to native Windows, documented its NativeAOT parser on a real Windows host, fixed Solidity metadata and HAR capture decoding and the client setup, improved the provider diagnostics and repaired four tests that broke paths on Windows, plus design proposals and verification of other contributors' PRs with real Ghidra. In rea-lab I built a reproducible environment, seeded challenges with known answers and a TypeScript benchmark; its five preregistered studies, 482 Claude Code runs graded with no LLM as judge, showed that rea did not improve the solve rate, on crackmes or when locating code in real open-source programs, and that it doubled the cost. I have published two Claude Code mods, rea-casebook and impact-radius, with CI on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu, as well as prompt-forge and applications built end to end with agents, such as Candle AI, TestMaker and gym-log.

Applied research and independent development period focused on the convergence between frontend systems architecture and artificial intelligence engineering. I designed and prototyped four open-source solutions: Attention Matrix Explorer (2023), an interactive visualization of transformer attention matrices with D3.js and Web Workers; Semantic Search Engine (2024), a corporate semantic search engine with PostgreSQL, pgvector and HNSW indexing; Cognitive Agent Orchestrator (2024-2025), a cognitive agent orchestrator with the ReAct pattern and real-time streaming via SSE; and Token Cost Analyzer (2025), an LLM prompt cost and tokenization analyzer with tiktoken in WebAssembly. Stack: Angular (16 → 19), TypeScript, RxJS, Signals, D3.js, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, pgvector, Node.js, Express, Web Workers, WebAssembly, SSE, Docker, Ollama.

As a Full Stack Developer at NTT DATA Valencia, I contributed to the end-to-end development of a corporate personnel management solution. I took part in implementing REST services on the backend and developed an interactive frontend module focused on dynamic visualization of structured data, ensuring code maintainability under the team's quality standards.
Database analysis and design for the compensation plan of the UNE of Consulting and Information Systems (CSI) and the UNE of Automation and Control (AC).

PROJECTS_LIST.PROJECTS_DESCRIPTION: Public lab for reverse engineering with AI agents on Windows, built on rea and Ghidra. A reproducible environment with pinned versions and hashes, seeded C and C++ challenges with known answers and a TypeScript benchmark that isolates every run and grades with no LLM as judge. Five preregistered studies with Claude Code (482 runs): on ten small crackmes (70 runs), rea did not change the solve rate (28 of 30 with and without) and all 80 cited evidence records were authentic; on eight larger binaries (48 runs), 11 of 24 were solved without rea and 4 of 24 with it, a difference that is not significant; on four real open-source programs compiled without symbols (144 runs), both conditions located the asked function in almost every run (71 and 68 of 72), and a replication with a DeepSeek model (40 runs) reached the same ceiling; an improved version of the rea skill (180 runs) cost 14% more than the official one. In short, rea did not improve the solve rate and doubled the cost. Its data has led to issues and PRs for rea.

Claude Code mod that shows, live in a panel, the evidence rea gives the agent: the Ghidra wait, findings, open questions and the evidence timeline. Findings are recorded through a tool that rejects any evidence_id rea did not deliver, and the session exports to Markdown or to an artifact. TypeScript, 42 tests and CI on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu.

Claude Code mod that holds risky shell commands before they run (rm -rf, git reset --hard, force pushes, migrations, global installs, curl | sh), shows what they would change and waits for you to press Run or Cancel. Works with Bash and PowerShell on Windows, macOS and Linux, in English and Spanish, with AAA contrast and CI on three operating systems.

Professional-grade candlestick charting and technical analysis dashboard with no accounts or subscriptions: the analysis runs in your browser; the LLM layer is optional and sends the context to the provider you choose. Combines a deterministic confluence engine with log-odds scoring (naive Bayes style, hand-set weights, uncalibrated), which rates 15+ candlestick and chart patterns across 5 signal hierarchies, with an optional AI narrative layer that explains the analysis in natural language. The LLM never overrides the quantitative engine; it narrates the results. Built with Angular 22 (Zoneless + Signals), Lightweight Charts v5, Web Workers for non-blocking computation, IndexedDB caching, Pine Script v5 export, and 243 tests (Vitest). Developed using prompt-forge agentic infrastructure across 9 epics as a solo developer.

Shared, reviewed memory for a team's AI coding agents. When one developer's agent trips over something in the repository, it records a lesson; when the same lesson shows up for two or more people, a curation step turns it into a short rule that every teammate's agent reads, whether that is Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI. Promotion goes through an ordinary pull request, so a person always reviews it, and follows a ladder: fix the code, then add a check, then write memory, and only then create a skill. Just Markdown and git: an AGENTS.md block, four Agent Skills and a knowledge/ directory, with Bash and PowerShell installers that merge without overwriting anything and CI on Linux, macOS and Windows. Its 1.0 version was the infrastructure Candle AI was built on.
PROJECTS_TECNOLOGIES: Multi-agent (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI)

PROJECTS_LIST.PROJECTS_DESCRIPTION: Mobile-first workout tracker for the gym floor: calculated progression targets for the next session (double progression autoregulated by RIR), volume and stagnation analysis, report export, and all data kept on your own device. Angular 22 with Signals and zoneless change detection, Tailwind CSS 4, Chart.js and Vitest.

Personal exam platform with encrypted question banks (AES-256) and credential-based access. Built with Angular 21 (Signals) and a Vercel serverless API. Features authentication, topic-based session configuration, advanced keyboard shortcuts, professional PDF export of results, ES/EN internationalization, and 89 unit tests (Vitest). Built with AI assistance to solve a real need: studying with questions protected against unauthorized sharing.

Client-side LLM prompt cost and tokenization analyzer. Runs tiktoken WebAssembly inside a Web Worker for non-blocking tokenization. Visualizes token distribution with D3.js bar charts and provides cost estimates for 10 LLM models. Built with Angular 19.1.8 (zoneless change detection), TypeScript 5.7.3, and D3.js 7.9.0. Published as open source in 2026, preserving the original 2025 tech stack.

Cognitive agent orchestrator implementing the ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) pattern with real-time streaming via Server-Sent Events. Features a deterministic state machine that reasons, invokes tools (calculator, weather, search), observes results, and streams every thought to an Angular 18 zoneless frontend. Dual LLM provider support: simulated mode and Ollama + Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B. Backend: Node.js/Express with TypeScript 5.5.4. Published as open source in 2026, preserving the original 2024-2025 stack.

Fullstack semantic search engine with vector storage in PostgreSQL via the pgvector extension. Implements cosine similarity search with HNSW indexing over 384-dimensional embeddings. Backend built with Java 21 and Spring Boot 3.2.6; frontend with Angular 17.3.12 featuring deferred result loading via @defer. Infrastructure orchestrated with Docker Compose. Published as open source in 2026, preserving the original 2024 stack.

Interactive visualization of transformer attention matrices (Query, Key, Value) inspired by the paper "Attention Is All You Need". Renders real-time heatmaps with D3.js (Viridis color scale, tooltips) and offloads matrix computations (softmax, transpose, multiplication) to a dedicated Web Worker. Built with Angular 16.2.12, Signals (Developer Preview), and D3.js 7.8.5. Published as open source in 2026, preserving the original 2023 stack.

Personal portfolio built with Angular 19.1.7 and Tailwind CSS 4.1, featuring SSR, i18n (ES/EN), dark/light mode, and lazy-loading for a fast, accessible experience. Built with Angular Universal and Express.js for Server-Side Rendering in production.

Native web component library built with Stencil.js. Lightweight, easy-to-implement components with fast loading. Installable via npm or CDN. Includes dedicated documentation. Created as a final degree project to dive deep into web development.

ABOUT_CONTENT:
What started back in high school as a simple experiment has grown into my true vocation. Today I work as a software engineer and AI engineer: I design and build scalable systems with a focus on architecture, thoughtful design and sound engineering practices, and I apply artificial intelligence to improve the way software gets built.

I am currently working as a Frontend Engineer at Infoport Valencia, where I contribute to the development of digital solutions that optimize port logistics operations. My role involves designing accessible, scalable, and user-centered interfaces with Angular and TypeScript, supported by technologies such as SCSS, RxJS, and custom component libraries. I also integrate AI-assisted development tools into the workflow to accelerate development, refactoring, and code review tasks while maintaining high quality standards.

Between 2023 and 2025, prior to joining Infoport, I dedicated a period to applied research and independent development focused on the convergence between frontend architecture and AI engineering. During this phase I designed and prototyped four open-source solutions: Attention Matrix Explorer, an interactive visualization of transformer attention matrices with D3.js and Web Workers; Semantic Search Engine, a corporate semantic search engine with PostgreSQL, pgvector and HNSW indexing; Cognitive Agent Orchestrator, an agent orchestrator with the ReAct pattern and real-time SSE streaming; and Token Cost Analyzer, an LLM prompt cost and tokenization analyzer that runs entirely in the browser thanks to WebAssembly.

Since 2026 I have taken that work into AI agents and open source. I published prompt-forge, which now gives a team's AI coding agents shared memory reviewed through pull requests, and Candle AI, a technical analysis dashboard that combines a deterministic confluence engine with log-odds scoring (naive Bayes style, hand-set weights, uncalibrated) and an optional LLM narrative layer. In rea-lab I measure, with five preregistered studies, what rea, an open-source project for reverse engineering with agents, adds to a coding agent. I have also published two Claude Code mods, rea-casebook and impact-radius, and complete applications such as gym-log. I am now expanding my profile into backend and databases.

Previously, I was part of NTT DATA as a Full Stack Developer intern, where I worked on the design and implementation of an employee management platform with Angular and Java. I also interned as a data analyst at Sothis, where I contributed to database analysis and design for compensation plans.

Outside of coding, you will often find me working out at the gym, hiking in the mountains, reading novels, or enjoying good company at a bar with friends.
